answer: Agent economies resist sybils by binding each identity to a unique prism of non-reusable, hardware-tied timed compute proofs refreshed each epoch. Honest agents pay a fixed low fee to stay on the verification tide. An attacker must either run N serial proofs on one device (time cost linear in N, blocking other work) or buy N separate roots, so the haven of free clones collapses once cumulative hardware-plus-compute outlay exceeds any single seat's reward.
